{{unsolved|mathematics|Does forbidding both a tree and a clique as induced subgraphs produce graphs of bounded chromatic number?}}
In [[graph theory]], the '''Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture''' says that for any fixed [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] <math>T</math>, the class of all  <math>T</math>-free graphs is [[χ-bounded|<math>\chi</math>-bounded]]{{r|s97}}; that is, every graph that contains neither <math>T</math> nor <math>K_t</math> as an [[induced subgraph]] can be [[graph coloring|properly colored]] using a constant number of colors, depending only on <math>T</math> and <math>t</math>.
Equivalently, it says that every <math>K_t</math>-free graph <math>G</math> contains any arbitrarily chosen tree <math>T</math> (as an induced subgraph), as long as <math>\chi(G)</math> is large enough.
It is named after [[András Gyárfás]] and [[David Sumner]], who formulated it independently in 1975 and 1981 respectively.{{r|g75|s81}} It remains unproven.{{r|cs14}}

In this conjecture, it is not possible to replace <math>T</math> by a graph with cycles. As [[Paul Erdős]] and [[András Hajnal]] have shown, there exist graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number and, at the same time, arbitrarily large [[girth (graph theory)|girth]].{{r|eh66}} Using these graphs, one can obtain graphs that avoid any fixed choice of a cyclic graph and clique (of more than two vertices) as induced subgraphs, and exceed any fixed bound on the chromatic number.{{r|s97}}

The conjecture is known to be true for certain special choices of <math>T</math>, including [[path graph|paths]],{{r|g87}} [[star (graph theory)|stars]], and trees of radius two.{{r|kp94}}
It is also known that, for any tree <math>T</math>, the graphs that do not contain any [[Homeomorphism (graph theory)|subdivision]] of <math>T</math> are <math>\chi</math>-bounded.{{r|s97}}
